summary:
The Accelerating Appraisals and Conservation Efforts Act, Pub. L. No. 118-230, establishes a Department of the Interior appraisal licensing rule for real property transactions within the jurisdiction of the Secretary of the Interior. Section 1 provides the short title and is codified as a note to 43 U.S.C. § 1451.

Section 2, codified at 43 U.S.C. § 1478, provides that a “covered appraiser”—defined as a State-licensed or State-certified real property appraiser—need be licensed or certified in only one State to perform appraisal or valuation services for real property in any State for a transaction over which the Secretary has jurisdiction. If the Secretary uses a non-Federal covered appraiser, the Secretary must, to the maximum extent practicable, use a certified general real property appraiser licensed in a State where the subject real property is located. The Secretary may use a certified general real property appraiser licensed in another State only upon a determination that an in-State non-Federal covered appraiser is unavailable to complete the assignment within a reasonable period, is not assignment qualified, or is not cost competitive.

Section 2(c) requires the Secretary, not later than one year after enactment and annually thereafter for at least four additional years, to submit reports to Congress comparing request volumes and completion times before and after enactment; assessing the effect of the one-State licensure rule on contracting flexibility; providing any recommendations for congressional action; summarizing the Department’s appraisal and valuation workforce, including employees and contractors; and listing each case in which the Act’s authority was used, with the criteria applied.

Section 2(d) preserves the application of Federal and State laws and regulations to non-Federal covered appraisers except as expressly provided, and clarifies that the Act does not authorize appraisal or valuation services in a State where the appraiser is not licensed or certified except for transactions within the Secretary’s jurisdiction. It further provides that any Federal or State law or regulation enacted before enactment requiring licensure or certification in a specific State does not apply to such transactions.

Section 2(e) requires, within 90 days after enactment, online public availability and availability upon request of Department policies, manuals, guidance, handbooks, standard operating procedures, and policy statements specific to scoping, contracting, and review of appraisals performed for the Department by Federal or non-Federal covered appraisers. The Act contains no authorization of appropriations or direct appropriation.
